title: Senior Manager, CX Messaging and Activation Lead
description:
At Pfizer, our purpose is breakthroughs that change patients' lives. As we implement our AI Transformation, our GTM and Adoption team helps turn digital investment into real impact by understanding and removing barriers, driving high-impact engagement, and ensuring the new digital platforms we launch become embedded into how our colleagues work.
  
  
This is a product marketing role. The products are internal AI platforms. The market is roughly 80,000 Pfizer colleagues around the world. Positioning, segmentation, launch, and demand generation all apply here, with adoption and retention as the scoreboard.
  
  
The craft at the center of the role is positioning: holding one argument per platform and telling it in many ways. A scientist in the lab, a supervisor on a manufacturing line, and an analyst in finance should each recognize their own work in the same value proposition, and a colleague who has never heard of a platform needs something different from one who tried it once and stopped. Working norms, language, and attitudes toward AI at work also differ across our markets and business lines, so messaging here is adapted for the audience rather than translated once and sent everywhere. What we are claiming stays constant. How it is told, to whom, and at what point in their journey is where this role does its work.
  
  
This role translates technical features into highly compelling, user-centric narratives, running internal product launches with the same rigor, creativity, and brand building typically reserved for external consumer technology launches. Most internal launch emails and mandatory announcements get ignored, and that's the bar this role is here to clear: before defaulting to the standard internal-comms playbook, this role tries something unconventional first, and builds campaigns around what actually earns attention rather than what's easiest to schedule.
  
  
**Positioning, Messaging & Segmentation**

* Segment by lifecycle stage rather than by org chart. Match messaging to where a colleague sits with a platform: one who has never heard of it needs a reason to care, one who tried it once and stopped needs a different reason to come back, and one who uses it weekly needs to know what changed.
* Build divisional and cultural understanding into the work. Language, regulatory context, working norms, and attitudes toward AI at work differ across markets and business lines, and a message that reads as exciting in one place can read as overselling or as a threat in another. Partner with divisional and local communicators so messaging is adapted rather than translated.
* Ground the WIIFM ("What’s In It For Me") in the colleague’s actual workday: the task that gets shorter, the handoff that stops breaking, the report nobody has to rebuild by hand. Avoid capability claims that do not name a job somebody is trying to get done.
* Own the competitive frame. Position each platform against what colleagues are choosing instead, whether an external consumer AI tool, a manual workaround, or doing nothing, and make the honest case for the internal option rather than assuming the audience is captive.
* Test messaging with real colleagues before it ships, in more than one division, and rewrite what does not land.
* Keep the message library current as platforms change, and retire claims that stop being true.

**Go-to-Market & Launch**

* Set the channel and audience strategy for each launch, deciding which channels to use and who to target, and own the resulting content end to end, creative through send.
* Coordinate channel and audience decisions with the Peer Advocacy & Community Lead so broadcast and community messaging reinforce each other rather than duplicate or conflict.
* Write the go-to-market plan for every major launch: target audience, messaging pillars in play, channel mix, sequencing, asset list, dates, and the adoption number the launch is meant to move. A launch is a plan on paper before it is a calendar invite.
* Run the pre-launch phase. Early access cohorts, waitlists, teasers, and champion previews build demand ahead of general availability so day one has an audience waiting rather than an audience being informed.
* Sequence the launch with the CX Training Lead and the Peer Advocacy & Community Lead so messaging, training readiness, and community activity land in the right order rather than competing on the same day.
* Run a post-launch review after every Major launch: what the campaign moved, what it did not, and what changes in the next one. Feed the pattern back into the reusable launch approach.

**Demand Generation & Funnel Ownership**

* Own the top of the funnel end to end, from unaware through interested to first use. Know the drop-off at each step, and fix the weakest step rather than adding more volume at the top.
* Build the always-on layer that runs between launches so demand does not depend on a campaign being live: placement on the surfaces colleagues already hit, internal search and intranet presence, the platform site, and the moments new joiners are most open to trying something.

**Enablement, Standards & Message Governance**

* Establish the reusable launch playbook: message standards, frameworks, and templates that later launches and other teams run on.
* Enable the people who carry the message. Equip stakeholders, champions, and divisional communicators with the positioning, proof points, and assets to make the case in their own words. This is sales enablement without a sales team.
* Facilitate knowledge sharing through communication channels that connect colleagues with successful practices, lessons learned, and success stories.
* Prepare colleagues for change by developing communication strategies that support adoption of new tools, workflows, and behaviors.

**Platform & Strategy Partnership**

* Partner closely with the Experience Architecture and Product teams to understand what each platform is and the CX strategy defined for it, so positioning and messaging stay grounded in the platform’s actual intent.
* Feed user insights, friction points, and feature requests surfaced through campaigns and interviews back to the teams building and evolving each platform.

**Ethical Use & Responsible AI Messaging**

* Define clear, plain-language guidance on the ethical and responsible use of each AI platform, appropriate use cases, data handling, and when to trust versus verify AI output, as part of launch and ongoing messaging.
* Shape that guidance in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and Regulatory Affairs so it stays accurate and consistent as platforms evolve.
* Share ethical-use guidance directly with the CX Training Lead so it gets built into training content, and with the Peer Advocacy & Community Lead so it is reinforced through the champion network and community norms.

**Legal & Regulatory Alignment**

* Own the legal, compliance, and regulatory review checkpoint for platform messaging, built into the launch timeline as a fast, repeatable step rather than a one-off cycle, so nothing overstates a platform’s capabilities, data handling, or compliance posture.
* Know which platforms touch regulated, clinical, or personal data, and keep messaging current with internal policy on AI-related communications.

**Producing the Work, Not Just Briefing It**

* Write, design, and produce the core campaign assets, launch copy, short-form video, key visuals, on a real production cadence.
* This is not a brief-an-agency-and-wait role; the person hired is expected to make the work themselves or partner internally with the design teams, especially in the early days of a launch when speed matters most.

**Campaign Metrics Tied to Real Adoption**

* Set quarterly targets for campaign metrics (click-throughs, video views, waitlist sign-ups), but treat none of them as the finish line.
* Ensure every campaign metric ladders up to the platform’s two core success metrics, 30-day active use and the Sean Ellis test.
* Partner with the Adoption Analytics & Insights Lead on the dashboard that shows that connection, not just the vanity numbers.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Digital Media, or a related field.
* 6–8+ years in product marketing, digital marketing, or brand strategy, with a highly creative portfolio. Product marketing for a software, SaaS, or platform product is the closest fit, whether the audience was external customers or internal users.
* Experience owning top-of-funnel performance, including awareness-to-first-use conversion and diagnosing where an audience drops off.
* Experience owning a product launch end to end, including go-to-market planning, launch tiering, pre-launch demand building, and post-launch review.
* Experience building a messaging architecture (pillars, proof points, persona-level messaging) for a product or platform and holding other teams to it.
* Experience establishing messaging standards, launch frameworks, or reusable practices that other teams, platforms, or business units adopt.
* Experience translating complex technical or AI capabilities into clear, persona-specific business benefits and messaging.
* Hands-on experience personally writing, designing, and producing campaign assets on areal production cadence, not only briefing and reviewing agency or vendor work.
* Experience defining launch tiers and orchestrating cross-functional launch timelines and communications.
* Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your own production work, with a clear view of where they help and where they fall short.
* Experience partnering with Legal, Compliance, or Regulatory teams to review communications before publication, ideally within a pharmaceutical, healthcare, or other regulated industry.
* Comfort tying campaign metrics (engagement, click-through, sign-ups) to downstream adoption and retention outcomes rather than treating them as the end goal.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in consumer tech, B2B SaaS, a creative agency, or another fast-paced digital marketing environment.
* Experience launching or positioning an AI product, or explaining AI capability and limitation to a non-technical audience.
* Proficiency with modern creative design and video editing tools.
* Experience driving engagement within enterprise collaboration tools (e.g., Teams, Slack, Viva Engage).
* Experience partnering with architecture, engineering, or technical teams to ground messaging in actual platform capability and strategy.
* Familiarity with pharmaceutical or healthcare industry communication standards (e.g., promotional review processes, data privacy requirements) as they apply to internal, employee-facing content.
* Experience partnering with learning and community counterparts to sequence messaging, training, and community activity into a single integrated launch plan.
* Experience preparing stakeholder groups for a change in how they work through audience-specific messaging.
* Experience developing or communicating responsible or ethical AI use guidance for an internal or external audience.
* Experience positioning a product against a free or already-preferred alternative and winning users back.
* Experience running message testing, user research, or win-loss style interviews to shape positioning before launch.

title: Director of AI Experience Design
description:
**About OpenLoop**
------------------

OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. Our telehealth support solutions are thoughtfully designed to streamline and simplify go-to-market care delivery for companies offering meaningful virtual support to patients across an expansive array of specialties, in all 50 states.

We are the digital health infrastructure powering modern medicine. Healthcare and non-healthcare brands use our white-label platform to launch, scale and run virtual and hybrid care without the operational complexity. We bring together one of the largest telehealth clinician networks in the country, nationwide payer coverage, integrated pharmacy and lab partners, EHR connectivity, 24/7 patient support and full revenue cycle management. Our partners put their brand on the front end, and everything behind it runs on us. We serve more than 3 million patients a year and power over 1 million visits a month.

**About the Role**
------------------

As **Director of AI Experience Design** at OpenLoop Health, you'll lead design across everything we build: patient and client-facing experiences, our White-Label platform and Launchpad, AI agents and copilots, and the operational platforms our teams use every day.

You'll set a multi-year design vision, grow and lead the team, and own the system our products are built on. That system won't only guide human designers. It becomes the contract AI follows, precise enough that AI tools can build UI that meets our bar. You'll also help designers, engineers, and PMs use AI effectively and at scale, so the team can do more without lowering the bar on quality.

You'll treat design like a business: own the outcomes, make focused bets, and iterate based on customer truth and data. This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of strategy and execution.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Set the design vision and strategy across patient, client, and internal products, and turn bold ideas into outcomes patients, clients, and the business can measure.
* Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of designers. Establish clear career paths, strong critique, and a culture with a high bar for craft.
* Own the design system as the source of truth, not a side artifact. That covers tokens, components, information hierarchy, and interaction principles, with theming across the many client brands our White-Label platform supports.
* Make the system AI-ready. Ship standards as code (tokens, patterns, and components wired into the engineering pipeline) so the correct, accessible, compliant pattern is the default for people and AI coding agents alike.
* Measure the system like a product, using adoption in code, pattern reuse, override rates, and first-pass quality, and retire patterns the data shows are failing.
* Help the Product & Tech org use AI effectively and at scale, with the workflows, tools, and standards that let the team ship more without sacrificing quality.
* Set the standard for how AI shows up in our products, across voice, chat, and autonomous agents. That covers trust patterns like transparency, citations, confidence, error recovery, escalation, and human handoff in a regulated healthcare setting.
* Ground decisions in research. Run discovery and usability testing with patients, clinicians, and clients, and prototype in code with real data to validate ideas before they scale.
* Audit existing and acquired surfaces, such as Hey Revia and Season Health, and drive convergence toward a single coherent experience.
* Partner with Product and Engineering leaders on problem definition, roadmap, and scoping.
* Own design KPIs and instrument the experience to quantify impact. Represent Design in executive forums with clear narratives, tradeoffs, and results.

**Who You Are**
---------------

* 10+ years in product design, with 3+ years leading teams directly. B2B or B2B2C SaaS experience preferred.
* A portfolio showing end-to-end systems thinking, exceptional craft, and shipped work at scale across web and mobile.
* A track record of designing and shipping AI-powered or agentic experiences in production, and of changing how teams and AI tools actually build.
* Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain great design talent.
* Inspired by products where systematic design creates clarity, and you know what separates great product experiences from good ones.
* Meticulous and opinionated, able to hold the line on standards while moving fast.
* Comfortable being both hands-on (Figma, tokens, specs, prototyping in code with tools like Claude Code) and strategic (principles, governance, cross-team alignment).
* A strong command of accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) and of designing for trust in high-stakes settings.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, able to align executives around crisp narratives and metrics.
* Healthcare or other regulated-industry experience is a plus.

**Our Benefits**
----------------

In addition, for salaried positions you would also be eligible for:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision plans
* Flexible Spending/Health Savings Accounts
* Flexible PTO
* 401(k) + Company Match
* Life Insurance, Pet insurance, and more

**Our Company**
---------------

We have a relatively flat organizational structure here at OpenLoop. Everyone is encouraged to bring ideas to the table and make things happen. This fits in well with our core values of Autonomy, Competence and Belonging, as we want everyone to feel empowered and supported to do their best work.

Sound like a good fit? We’d love to meet you.

****Role Objective****
****AtlasBrands is looking for a Head of Performance Creative (Meta) to serve as the "CEO" of our primary acquisition channel.****
Because Meta represents 100% of our customer growth, you will take complete, end-to-end ownership of the channel and leading with an obsessive, direct-response creative strategy while cross-functionally overseeing media buying execution.
  
  
You are a world-class performance creative lead who stays deeply in the trenches, studying market trends and competitor ads to craft high-converting hooks and concepts. Your core objective is to build and scale a pod-based creative department that powers rapid revenue expansion while maintaining strict unit economics, total account stability, and proactive resolution of ad rejections and account risk across high-risk verticals (e.g., supplements). * Brand Scaling Systems: Execute staged growth targets for existing brands at first-rebill break-even or better. Establish a standardized launch protocol for new brands to reach scale rapidly while maintaining a near-perfect success rate.
* Retention & Margin Optimization: Shift brands from first-rebill break-even to first-purchase break-even as they mature, sustaining performance month-over-month. Proactively flag risks ahead of time with actionable recovery plans.
* Ad Rejection & Account Health Management: Rapidly troubleshoot and resolve ad rejections, policy flags, and disablements inherent to high-risk verticals (e.g., supplements). Set up and manage redundant account architecture (backup BMs, ad accounts, payment methods) to guarantee zero downtime and keep spend scaling uninterrupted.

* Proven $100K+/Day Scale: Track record taking DTC brands to aggressive scale, directly responsible for managing $100K+ daily Meta ad spend across catalog depth (6–10+ distinct SKUs).
* Direct-Response Mastery & In-the-Trenches Mindset: Obsessed with studying winning market trends, analyzing competitor ads, and turning consumer psychology into high-velocity creative concepts.
* Operational Resilience in High-Risk Verticals: Hands-on experience resolving policy flags, ad rejections, and account risks in supplement/health categories while keeping spend live via backup account infrastructure.
* High-Tempo Work Ethic (50+ Hrs/Wk): Hyper-ambitious operator who thrives under high pressure, brings a history of 50+ hour work weeks, and wants to grind alongside an elite team pushing toward 9 figures.
* Full Channel Ownership & Execution: Operates as a true "CEO of Meta"—building A-player creative pods, overseeing media buying alignment, and executing with extreme speed and autonomy.
* AI-Driven Automation: Leverages modern LLMs (Claude, GPTs) and automated data workflows to streamline creative analysis, build tracking dashboards, and scale output.

****Working Hours & Culture****

* Role Timeline: Full-time leadership hire.
* Async-First: Global, remote-first team setup requiring core daily overlap with US EST business hours for team syncs and cross-functional alignment.

At AtlasBrands, we value your time and expertise, which is why we’ve built a streamlined, highly transparent interview process designed to look for a true partner rather than a transactional contributor.

We’re looking for a senior Growth Lead with deep expertise in brand and trade marketing to shape how Mexican consumers see our brand and to build our in-store acquisition channel. Your mission is not just to grow volume, but to grow the right customers: attracting higher-quality, lower-risk and more profitable cardholders for our Mexico Credit Card.
  
  
A big part of the opportunity is a channel few card issuers in Mexico are present in: in-store acquisition through our merchant partners. Physical retailers already distribute our cards at the point of sale, and the channel is largely untapped. We want someone who can turn it into a growth engine through trade marketing, in-store promotions, POP and co-marketing with our merchants.
  
  
You’ll also own our brand in Mexico: positioning, messaging and creative direction across socials, digital and in-store. You’ll work closely with our UK growth and analytics team, who lead performance marketing, tracking and attribution, and with our Credit team to make sure every campaign brings in customers who are good for the business.
  
  
This role is central to scaling our Mexico Credit Card, a mobile-app–first product designed for credit builders in Mexico.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Build Trade & Retail Marketing at the Point of Sale
* Own the growth strategy for our in-store acquisition channel with physical merchant partners.
* Build and run a trade marketing calendar with each merchant: promotions such as a free card with the purchase of selected products or above a spend threshold, in-store activations and brand ambassadors.
* Develop POP and in-store advertising, from concept to production and rollout across store networks, that drives awareness and sign-ups at the shelf and at checkout.
* Launch co-marketing campaigns with merchants through their own channels (apps, loyalty programs, catalogues, socials) and joint offers.
* Work with merchant partners, Operations and Engineering on execution: store staff incentives and training, systems integration and reconciliation of promotion costs.
* Build a repeatable playbook so we can launch new merchant partners quickly.
* Own & Build Our Brand in Mexico
* Own brand positioning, messaging and identity, shaping how Mexican consumers perceive us so we attract the customers we want to serve.
* Define creative direction and lead brand campaigns across socials, digital, out-of-home and in-store.
* Build a creative engine (in-house, agencies, creators) that produces high-quality assets at speed.
* Grow our organic social presence, content and community.
* Track brand health (awareness, consideration, perception) and connect brand work to acquisition results.
* Connect Brand, Retail & Digital
* Design digital-to-store campaigns with merchants that drive customers into stores to get their card (e.g. geo-targeted social, merchant channels).
* Keep the brand consistent across every touchpoint, and provide messaging and creative for our performance campaigns.
* Partner with the UK growth and analytics team, who own performance marketing execution, tracking and attribution, so brand and trade campaigns are properly measured and learnings flow both ways.
* Measure What Matters
* Own the brand and trade marketing budget, and the return on it.
* Define clear KPIs for every campaign and merchant: cost per account, approval and activation rates, and customer quality.
* Work with Credit and the UK analytics team to understand which campaigns, merchants and promotions bring in profitable customers, and how CAC compares to LTV.
* Use results to reallocate spend across merchants, promotions and campaigns.

**Required Experience**
**What We’re Looking For**

* 6+ years in brand, trade, retail or shopper marketing, with senior ownership of meaningful budgets and targets, ideally at consumer brands, retailers or financial services in Mexico.
* A proven track record of launching trade marketing and in-store campaigns with retailers: promotions, POP, activations and co-marketing.
* Experience building or repositioning a consumer brand: positioning, messaging, creative direction and campaigns.
* Strong experience working with and negotiating with Mexican retailers and their store teams.
* Experience managing creative, BTL and production agencies and vendors.
* Commercially minded and data-literate: comfortable setting KPIs, reading campaign results and tying spend to outcomes.
* Strong execution across many stakeholders (merchants, Operations, Finance, Credit).
* Proficiency in English and Spanish (you’ll work closely with our UK team).
* Deep understanding of Mexican consumers.

Nice to Have
  
  

* Experience in performance marketing across Meta, Google, TikTok or app marketing.
* Familiarity with tracking and data integrations, such as Meta Conversions API (CAPI), Google offline conversions, MMPs and attribution.
* Analytical skills such as SQL, cohort analysis or unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback).
* Experience in credit cards, lending or other financial services, ideally with an understanding of credit risk.
* Previous start-up or scale-up experience, ideally building a channel from zero.
* Experience leading a team.

**The Type of Work You’ll Be Doing**

* Plan and launch trade marketing promotions with merchant partners.
* Create POP and in-store materials, and roll them out across store networks.
* Negotiate co-marketing plans with merchants and onboard new partners.
* Define our brand positioning and lead brand campaigns.
* Brief and manage creative work, agencies and creators.
* Design digital-to-store campaigns with merchants.
* Review campaign and merchant performance with Credit and the UK analytics team, and reallocate budget.
* Report on growth performance to leadership and keep the team focused on what moves the needle.
* Help hire and build out the growth team as we scale.

**How You’ll Contribute To Zable**

* Ownership: You own brand and in-store acquisition end to end, from strategy and budget to results.
* Brand Building: You create a brand that Mexican consumers trust and want to be part of.
* Retail Savvy: You know how to win at the point of sale and how to work with retailers.

**Interview Process**

**Location**

description:

We are a nonprofit – passionate about revolutionizing the future of in-home care, and are looking for others to join our smart, collaborative and kind team.

  

**The Details:**

**In-Office Requirements:** This role requires up to 10% presence at our Downtown Seattle headquarters, Standard business hours Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

**Remote Work Eligibility:** For employees residing outside of the Seattle metropolitan area, remote work may be considered in the following states: AZ, CA, CO, ID, FL, OR, TN, VA, SC (Dorchester County) or WA. Final approval is determined through a management review process.

**Category:** Full-Time, FLSA Exempt, Regular, Non-Union

**About the Position:**

Reporting to the Senior Director of Benefits Operations, the Director of Plan Design and Program Management is accountable for executing, managing, and evaluating a comprehensive health and retirement plan strategy to improve quality and value of plan services and equitable access to benefits for plan members. This Director will seize opportunities that advance access, value, and quality of benefits by leveraging data to monitor health and retirement plan performance, identifying opportunities for improvement, and partnering with carriers and vendors to implement interventions that result in improved financial and wellness outcomes. title: Director of Energy Storage Modeling and Design
description:
### **ROLE OVERVIEW**

Pivot Energy is seeking a motivated individual to join our Technical Operations team and lead the company’s Energy Storage modeling and design. The role covers market analysis, technical vendor evaluation, pricing, modeling, sizing, and design recommendations for our storage (DC-coupled with PV solar and standalone storage) project pipeline. This role combines aspects of engineering, collaboration with finance, operations, and policy teams with a goal of deploying and optimizing our storage pipeline.

The Director will be responsible for technical analysis of all solar- plus-storage (DC-coupled) and standalone energy storage market opportunities, including optimal system sizing. The Director will work with the market strategy, policy, and finance teams on revenue modeling and financial analysis, and with Estimation, Procurement, and Commercial Operations to optimize CAPEX and OPEX. The role also works regularly with project development leads and cross-team leads in Project Development Origination, Grid Interconnection, Engineering, Finance, Delivery, O&M, and Asset Management.The Director will have the opportunity to identify and vet potential areas of new energy storage business development, such as new geographies, programs, incentives, or procurements.

This is an opportunity to join a small team in a fast-growing market at an exciting and expanding company. This position offers significant growth potential at a B Corporation with operations across the USA.

### **PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Develop and maintain MATLAB and Excel based revenue projections for solar plus storage and standalone storage projects by maintaining and / or creating new custom tools or using third-party applications
* Use internal Excel-based financial models, determine the cost and overall value of distribution-scale solar plus storage, and standalone storage projects
* Train internal personnel use energy modeling tools (MATLAB or third-party) with a goal of scaling Pivot’s ability to model storage projects and markets.
* Train, teach, guide, and collaborate with external personnel that will review our energy models, inputs, assumptions, equations, and code.
* Work with other Pivot teams on detailed modeling and design and on external quoting of storge model inputs including CAPEX and OPEX
* Support internal opportunity leads from the Commercial team to define project value and pricing terms to developer partners and for utility RFPs through market and project level modeling and design assumptions
* Work with key hardware and software vendors on technical evaluation, pipeline discussions, modeling assumptions, design, pricing, and equipment specifications to optimize project-level design
* Provide design direction including sizing and equipment selection to the Engineering team for project-level design and interconnection applications.
* Support the Market Strategy team in vetting potential new markets through quantitative analysis of sample projects
* Advance individual and team BESS knowledge through structured training, self-directed learning, and educational opportunities across Pivot.
* Build, manage and guide a small team of BESS experts consisting of engineering, analytics, modeling, and other expertise necessary to guide sound market and project decisions related to BESS.
* Support team members’ career growth by helping them think through the market drivers affecting BESS.
* Regularly document and share key insights from energy storage analysis process with relevant internal teams
* Track opportunities and analysis requests in Pivot’s CRM tools

### **REQUIRED COMPETENCIES**

Primary qualifications include demonstrated abilities to work collaboratively within a team, work collaboratively in cross team formats with other team leads, creatively solve quantitative problems, prioritize and manage a mix of short- and long-term deadlines, and professionally represent Pivot Energy externally. Experience in renewables and/or energy storage is required. The Director of Energy Storage Modeling and Design must be able to think critically and work with experienced renewables professionals to decipher the needs of a project/portfolio and find the best solutions in each scenario.

* Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (preferably Electrical Engineering with a focus on power system and energy system)
* Minimum 5 years of experience in the energy storage industry and storage project development
* Experience in the solar industry and solar project development
* Quantitative & qualitative problem-solving skills and strong communication skills
* Knowledge of renewable energy and project finance concepts
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple critical deadlines
* Passion for learning new things through self-directed study and structured settings
* High degree of proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially Excel
* Willingness to work in databases such as Salesforce

### **PREFERRED COMPETENCIES**

* Master’s degree in a relevant field
* At least 10 years of experience in the renewable energy industry
* Experience in energy trading, wholesale energy markets, or other energy economics disciplines
* Experience with Ascend Analytics, Fractal or similar energy modeling software
* Ability to create and modify energy models and finance models using MATLAB or a similar tool.

$160,000 - $190,000 a year

### **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

The base salary range for this position is $160,000-$190,000 depending on relevant experience, along with eligibility for the company’s substantial bonus plan, with a target bonus of 30% of annual salary (prorated in the first year based on start date).

  

Pivot Energy is dedicated to providing a great work experience for all employees, placing an emphasis on company culture and a focus on our people. To that end, Pivot offers an outstanding benefits package that includes:

* Excellent health/dental/vision insurance benefits with up to 100% of premiums covered by the company

* Company paid life insurance and short- & long-term disability coverage
* Generous parental leave

Pivot Energy is a national renewable energy provider that develops, finances, builds, owns, and manages solar and energy storage projects that help decarbonize our nation’s electricity, increase equitable access to clean energy for local communities, and provide real cost-savings to American businesses and

families.

We are fiercely dedicated to accelerating the rapid transition taking place in the energy industry to a more decentralized and cleaner approach to power generation. We are committed to positively contributing to the local communities and people we serve with more than clean energy. We believe global warming poses an existential threat to our planet and that we have a responsibility to help mitigate the threat. As a Certified B Corporation and one of **Denver’s “Best Places to Work”****,** we believe that company success is driven by a healthy environment, thriving society, and workplace where all individuals are respected. At Pivot, we are proactively developing and maintaining an inclusive culture, rooted in mutual respect, that supports a workforce of different generations, races, gender identities, sexual orientations, ability statuses, religions, and cultures to work collaboratively together for greater impact. description:
**Job Type:** Full-time **| Location:** San Francisco **| Department:** Procurement **| Reporting to:** VP, Data Center Procurement **|****Work Location Type:** #hybrid

The Senior Director, Sourcing & Procurement will own the end-to-end sourcing, contracting, and commercial
  
management strategy for General Contractor (GC), Architecture/Engineering (AE) design consultant, Substation EPC, and Commissioning (Cx) agent services supporting the company's U.S. hyperscale and AI-infrastructure data center construction program. This role is the primary procurement authority across the pre-construction, GC selection, sub trade selection, substation EPC, and commissioning phases of new-build and expansion projects, partnering closely with Construction, Engineering, Development, Legal, and Finance to secure capacity, control cost and schedule risk, and drive consistent, defensible contracting outcomes across a fast-growing portfolio of data center campuses.

  
  

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

  

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

  

Sourcing & Contracting Strategy

* Develop and execute global sourcing strategy for General Contractor, sub trades, Design-Build, and CMAR partners across shell/core, fit-out, and EPC substation scopes for U.S. data center builds.
* Lead procurement of AE/design consultant services (civil, structural, MEP, electrical distribution, low-voltage) and third-party Commissioning (Cx) agents across all project phases (Cx, IST, and turnover).
* Structure and negotiate contracts under GMP, lump sum, CMAR, Design-Build, and Progressive Design-Build models, tailoring commercial structure to project risk profile, schedule urgency, and market capacity.
* Build and maintain a qualified bench of regional and national GC, MEP, AE, and Cx partners to secure capacity ahead of an aggressive, multi-site construction pipeline.

Substation EPC

* Lead sourcing and contracting of Substation EPC scope (utility-interconnect and on-site substations), including transformers, switchgear, protection and controls, and interconnection-related civil/electrical works.
* Coordinate substation EPC procurement timelines with utility interconnection studies, HV transformer lead times, and GC construction sequencing to protect energization milestones.
* Negotiate substation EPC contracts and manage EPC contractor performance across design, procurement, and construction phases, including interface management with the GC and utility.

Cost, Risk & Schedule Management

* Own construction cost negotiations and benchmarking across GC/EPC scopes, including GMP validation, change order governance, and open-book cost reconciliation.
* Partner with Legal and Risk on contract terms covering liquidated damages, bonding/insurance, indemnification, OFCI/CFCI/ODCI scope delineation, and warranty obligations.
* Monitor project schedules jointly with Construction Management to identify sourcing risk (labor, equipment, long-lead materials) and proactively mitigate GC/Cx-driven schedule slippage.
* Track and report portfolio-level spend, savings, and contract compliance to procurement and executive leadership.

Cross-Functional Leadership

* Serve as the primary procurement business partner to Construction, Engineering, and Development leadership from site selection through project turnover.
* Represent Procurement in GC/AE/Cx/Substation EPC bid evaluations, contract award recommendations, and executive steering committee reviews.
* Build and mentor a team of category managers and buyers supporting the GC, design consultant, substation EPC, and commissioning categories as the portfolio scales.
* Establish standardized RFP templates, evaluation scorecards, and contract playbooks to drive consistency and speed across a growing project portfolio.

  

* 10+ years of progressive procurement, construction management, or supply chain leadership experience in hyperscale or mission-critical data center construction; prior experience at a hyperscaler, colocation provider, or major GC/EPC firm strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated command of GC/EPC sourcing, AE/design consultant procurement, Substation EPC contracting, and third-party commissioning agent engagement for large-scale data center or industrial facility builds. Deep working knowledge of GMP, lump sum, CMAR, Design-Build, and Progressive Design-Build contracting models, and of OFCI/CFCI/ODCI scope structuring.
* Strong grounding in construction cost negotiations, project scheduling interdependencies, and Substation EPC and shell/core/fit-out delivery.
* Proven track record negotiating complex, high-value construction and professional services contracts, with sound judgment on risk allocation and commercial structuring.
* Bachelor's degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.
* Willingness and ability to travel to active construction sites across the U.S. as needed

title: Director of Brand Design
description:
**About Cardiff**

Cardiff lends to small businesses. Since 2004 we've funded more than $12 billion across the country, to businesses in logistics, healthcare, construction, professional services, and plenty in between. We're building our own underwriting technology, and we still answer the phone; our customers need capital fast, and they want a straight answer from a person who can actually help.

**Location:** San Diego, CA or Remote (U.S.)

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Department:** Product and Design/Marketing

**Reports to:** CMO

**Why This Role Matters**

Our customers are small business owners who need capital quickly and clearly. Every screen, form, and message they see shapes whether they trust us enough to apply, finish, and come back. As Director of Brand Design, you'll set the standard for how Cardiff looks, feels, and works across our product, our brand, and every customer touchpoint, and you'll build the team and design system that keep that standard high as we grow.

**What You'll Own**

  

* Set the design vision and strategy for Cardiff's customer-facing products, internal tools, and brand, in partnership with Engineering, Marketing, and leadership
* Lead end-to-end product design for the borrower journey, from first visit and application through underwriting, funding, and repeat borrowing
* Design internal tools for our underwriting, funding, sales, and servicing teams so they can move faster with fewer errors
* Build and maintain a scalable design system in Figma, with documented components, patterns, and accessibility standards that engineering can ship from directly
* Own brand and visual identity across web, paid media, email, direct mail, and sales materials, partnering closely with Marketing on campaign creative
* Ground design decisions in evidence through customer research, usability testing, funnel analytics, and split testing, with clear metrics tied to conversion and customer experience
* Ensure designs meet accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) and the disclosure and compliance requirements of a regulated lending business
* Hire, lead, and develop the design team, running a predictable cadence of critique, delivery, and accountability
* Use AI tools throughout the design process, from research synthesis to prototyping, and help the team do the same

**What We're Looking For**

* **Experience:** 8+ years of product design experience, with at least 3 years leading designers and owning design outcomes for a digital product at a growth-stage company. Experience in fintech, lending, or financial services is a strong plus.
* **Product Design Craft:** A portfolio that shows strong interaction design, visual design, and information architecture on complex, multi-step flows such as applications, onboarding, or dashboards.
* **Design Systems:** Hands-on experience building and scaling a design system, and working closely with engineers to implement it in code.
* **Tools:** Expert-level Figma skills, fluency with prototyping and AI-assisted design tools, and a working knowledge of HTML, CSS, and how front-end code gets built.
* **Research and Data:** Comfort running user research and usability tests, and reading product analytics to find friction and measure the impact of design changes.
* **Leadership Style:** Hands-on, execution-focused leader with strong cross-functional communication skills; able to give clear feedback, make decisions with incomplete information, and explain design choices to non-designers. **Must have experience managing at least 4 direct reports.**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* **Industry Perspective:** Experience designing for small business owners, B2B customers, or regulated, high-trust products such as lending, payments, or banking.
* **Conversion Design:** A track record of improving funnel conversion, application completion, or activation through measured design changes.
* **Brand Leadership:** Experience leading a brand refresh or building a visual identity system that works across product and marketing channels.
* **Content Design:** Skill at writing and shaping clear product copy, especially for financial terms, disclosures, and error states.
* **Organizational Scale:** Experience building a design function at an early or growth-stage company, including hiring, career leveling, and managing freelance and agency partners.

**This Role May Not Be a Fit If You**

* Want a strategy or advisory seat rather than hands-on ownership of the work that ships
* Have been out of the tools long enough that you'd need someone else to build the file or the prototype
* Prefer structured corporate environments with clear lanes and layers between you and the business
* Solve problems offline and come back with polished results, instead of sharing work early and communicating while you work
* Use AI tools to assist your old workflow, rather than having rebuilt your workflow around them

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Base salary range: $195,000+
* Performance bonus of up to 20% of base, tied to delivery and business outcomes
* Medical, dental, and vision coverage
* 401(k) plan
* Flexible PTO and observed holidays
* Remote-first, with support for your home-office setup
* Direct access to leadership and to the problems that matter

title: Lead Product Manager, Consumer Experience
description:
**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $750M in bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for home services: three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome), one shared platform.

**About Product at LawnStarter**

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service experience for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

**About Consumer Experience at LawnStarter**

Hundreds of thousands of households book outdoor services through LawnStarter. Most come for mowing. The opportunity is everything that comes after: helping them discover what else we can do, and giving them every reason to stay.

That’s the opportunity. The customer web portal and app shapes everything after the first booking: how customers schedule, what they learn about their property, which services they find next, and whether they stay. Much of this experience has never had a dedicated owner, and retention is the biggest lever we haven’t pulled yet.

We believe AI changes what’s possible here. Instead of one product for everyone, we can build an outdoor-services experience tailored to each household: their yard, their schedule, and what they need next.

**The Role**

You’ll own the end-to-end consumer experience, after first booking through the lifetime of the customer relationship, and decide how AI shapes it. You’ll set the vision and roadmap for this area, then ship it alongside engineers, designers, data/ applied science partners, marketing, and operations.

As Lead PM, you’re an individual contributor operating with Lead-level scope: you own a full product area, build vision and strategy, set direction others build around, and work closely with the PM who owns the Pro experience so every customer win holds up on both sides of the marketplace. You’ll report to the Sr. Director of Product.

**What makes this role different:**

* You own the relationship, not a screen. Onboarding, scheduling, cross-sell, cancellation and win-back all sit with you, so you fix the whole journey, not one step.
* Room to define the product. These surfaces are live, yet much of the experience has never had a dedicated owner.
* AI is the strategy, not a feature. You'll decide where agentic and AI-based experiences help customers, then ship them.

**What You'll Own**

* **Onboarding**: From the first booking to a customer who trusts us with their yard.
* **Search and discovery**: Helping customers find what they need, including services they didn't know we offer.
* **Property details**: What shapes the service a customer gets and what a Pro walks into.
* **Scheduling**: Skips, reschedules, and frequency changes.
* **Reviews and tips**: How customers rate and reward their Pros.
* **Cancellations and win-back**: The moment a customer decides to leave, and the path back.
* **Cross-sell and personalization**: The right services for each customer, tailored to their household.
* **AI across the experience**: How AI enables all of the above, toward a customized outdoor-services product for every customer.

**Problems to Solve:**

**Turning a mowing customer into a household that trusts us for more.**  
Most customers come to us for one service and rarely see what else their yard needs. You’ll change that by building a deep understanding of each property and household (its size, condition, seasons, and what the customer cares about) and turning it into a personalized plan for everything outside the home. Discovery, search, and recommendations should feel like expert advice from someone who knows their yard, not a sales pitch. Get it right and customers trust us with more; get it wrong and we spend that trust.

**Keeping customers through the moments that make them leave.**  
Customers try to skip or reschedule a visit and get it wrong. Some cancel before their first service is ever done. Others leave months in. You'll remove scheduling friction, rethink the cancellation moment, and give departing customers a real reason to return.

**Setting the right expectations on both sides.**

Every service starts with a set of expectations: what the customer thinks they’re getting, and what the Pro thinks they’re walking into. When those don’t match, both sides lose. You’ll build the product that gets them aligned, combining what customers tell us, what Pros learn on the job, and what our proprietary data already knows about a property, so the right information reaches the right side before the visit happens. Get it right and services go smoothly, prices hold up, and both customers and Pros come back.

**Deciding where AI belongs, and shipping it responsibly.**  
Not every surface gets better with AI. You'll judge where agentic and AI-based features improve the consumer experience and where they add noise, then ship the ones that earn their place to hundreds of thousands of customers. At that scale, responsible means knowing how a feature fails before customers find out.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

* Consumer Retention, LTV, and CSAT go up: Measurable gains in customer retention, lifetime value (LTV), and satisfaction (CSAT).
* Pros come out even or ahead: Your customer-side wins have a neutral or positive effect on Pros.
* A vision the company rallies behind: A clear 1–2 year vision for the consumer experience, grounded in what our customers need and aligned with leadership.
* A roadmap that ships: A strong 6-12 month roadmap, executed and delivered.

  
**Requirements**

**Who You Are:**

**Experience**: 6+ years as a product manager on consumer-facing products, including at least one B2C product at scale.

**A track record of extraordinary outcome**s. Not solid, exceptional: results with your fingerprints on the decision. A generically solid resume, or wins you can't explain, won't clear the bar.

**An AI builder.** You've launched AI-powered consumer products and watched real people use them, so you know where AI makes an experience better and where it gets in the way. If you've never built an agentic or AI-based consumer experience, this role is unlikely to be a good fit.

**Customer-obsessed**. You go looking for consumer problems in reviews, support conversations, and funnel data. A confusing reschedule flow bothers you until it's fixed. This is unlikely to be a good fit if customers and their problems aren't what holds your attention.

**A systems thinker.** You see a product change as one part of a larger system and think through its second- and third-order effects before you ship. Here, that system is a marketplace: a change for customers almost always touches Pros, pricing, and operations too. You plan for those effects in the spec, not after launch. Marketplace experience helps, but what matters most is that you instinctively ask, “What else does this change?”.

**Experienced in personalization**. You've delivered personalized experiences before and know what it takes to make a product feel built for one household. This is unlikely to be a good fit if personalization, to you, means putting a first name in an email.

**A strategist who works from data and with design**. You set priorities and defend them. Product analytics, funnel analysis, and retention cohorts are your daily tools, so you diagnose why conversion drops deeper in the funnel instead of guessing. And you partner closely with design. If you need someone else to pull your numbers or hand you finished designs, this is unlikely to be a good fit.  
  
Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, engineering, design, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 6+ years of product management experience on consumer-facing products.

**This Role Is NOT:**

* **A people-management role**. You're an individual contributor with no direct reports. Influence comes from judgment and output, not a team you manage.
* **For someone who hasn't launched a B2C product at scale**. If you haven't shipped a consumer product to a large audience, please don't apply.
* **A data PM or platform PM role**. You'll lean on data and platforms daily but won't build them. Data and platform PMs are not a good fit.
* **A role with a big team and a clean stack**. We’re frugal and resourceful: a lean engineering team, a partly legacy stack, and seasonal tests that can take months to read. You’ll get impact by choosing carefully, using AI to move faster than headcount alone allows, and helping us understand what our data doesn’t yet tell us.
* **A strategy-only seat**. You'll write evals, read transcripts, and prototype with LLMs. If you'd rather just set direction, this will frustrate you.
* **A tactical delivery role**. This one owns where the consumer experience goes, not the next feature in it. If you're strongest turning someone else's strategy into tickets, this isn't the fit.

  
**Benefits**

* **Equity**: We want our product managers to benefit from significant company growth, so equity is a meaningful part of how we structure PM compensation.
* **Base salary**: $180,000 to $210,000
* **Healthcare**: Medical, dental, and vision
* **Location**: Fully remote (US). Deep thinking time and partnership with peers in engineering, design, data, marketing, and ops matter more than a desk.
* **PTO**: Flexible - We focus on results. Take what you need.

*LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.*

title: Director of Brand Media
description:
**Director of Brand Media**

**About MVR**

MVR Digital is a performance marketing agency helping emerging brands grow profitably. We bring together paid media, creative, and measurement to help clients make better marketing decisions and turn investment into business growth.

**About This Role**

As Director of Brand Media, you will lead brand media strategy across MVR’s client portfolio. You’ll help clients determine where to invest across linear TV, connected TV, out-of-home, audio, and digital channels, and how to evaluate those investments.

You’ll connect brand objectives with audience insights, creative direction, and media planning. Working alongside our Head of Paid Media and channel specialists, you’ll build plans that connect awareness and consideration to customer acquisition and revenue.

You will own the strategic recommendation: which audiences to reach, which channels to use, how much to invest, and what we should learn before expanding.

**Brand Media Strategy and Planning**

* Develop integrated media strategies across linear TV, CTV and streaming, OOH and digital billboards, online video, audio, programmatic display, and other relevant channels.Translate client business goals into audience priorities, channel recommendations, geographic plans, budgets, and campaign timing.
* Determine when a client is ready to expand into brand media, considering budget, creative, measurement readiness, and growth opportunities.
* Evaluate reach, frequency, audience overlap, and channel costs to recommend an effective media mix.
* Partner with creative teams to shape briefs, messages, and formats that fit the audience and placement.
* Identify and evaluate new media opportunities, sponsorships, and partnerships.

  

**Investment and Partner Management**

* Own brand media budget recommendations and allocation across channels and markets.
* Build investment scenarios that explain tradeoffs, expected outcomes, and the evidence behind each recommendation.
* Select and manage buying partners, publishers, and specialist agencies. Lead negotiations around pricing, inventory, placement quality, and added value.
* Oversee delivery with internal teams and external partners, addressing pacing, quality, and performance issues.
* Recommend when to scale, adjust, or stop an investment.

  

**Measurement and Business Impact**

* Define campaign objectives, KPIs, and measurement plans before launch.
* Partner with analytics specialists and measurement providers on brand-lift studies, incrementality tests, and marketing mix modeling.
* Use Northbeam or comparable tools alongside sales, CRM, and campaign data to understand how brand activity contributes to downstream results.  
  Interpret MMM findings and translate them into channel and budget decisions.
* Evaluate changes in brand awareness, consideration, branded search, qualified traffic, acquisition, and revenue without assuming that correlation proves impact.
* Explain what is working, what remains uncertain, and what the team should test next.

  

**Client Leadership and Collaboration**

* Serve as MVR’s senior brand media advisor in client planning sessions, presentations, and business reviews.
* Bring proactive recommendations grounded in each client’s economics, customer behavior, and growth priorities.
* Partner with the Head of Paid Media to coordinate brand investment with paid search, paid social, and other performance channels.
* Work with creative, client success, and project management to align briefs, launches, and reporting.
* Support new business pitches and help define MVR’s brand media offering.
* Mentor team members and develop repeatable planning standards. Keep decisions, owners, and deliverables documented in ClickUp.

  

**What You Bring**

* Eight or more years of experience in media strategy, planning, or investment, including senior responsibility for client or brand strategy.
* Experience leading integrated campaigns across traditional and digital media, including TV, CTV, and OOH.
* A track record of managing substantial media budgets and explaining how investment decisions supported business results.
* Experience planning for US audiences and navigating US media partners and buying practices.
* Strong understanding of brand building and how it works alongside performance marketing.
* Experience applying MMM, brand-lift, attribution, and incrementality findings to media decisions.
* Confidence evaluating agencies, negotiating with partners, and challenging recommendations.
* Clear client communication, strong presentation skills, and experience collaborating with creative and performance teams.
* Agency experience across multiple clients, familiarity with Northbeam, and experience helping brands expand beyond search and social are especially valuable.

  

**What Success Looks Like**

Clients understand where to invest, why MVR recommends it, and how we’ll judge the results. Creative and media teams work from a shared plan. You identify ineffective spending, recognize promising opportunities, and help clients make informed decisions about scaling brand media.

Within your first 90 days, you will assess priority clients, identify suitable brand media opportunities, and develop an initial investment and measurement plan. For an approved opportunity, you’ll align partners, creative requirements, and launch timing with the team.

title: Director, Health Policy and Reimbursement Strategy
description:
California, US residents .

**The job details are as follows:**

Who We Are

We are the first publicly-traded biotech or pharmaceutical company to take the form of a public benefit corporation. Our public benefit purpose is to provide a brighter future for patients through the development of novel pharmaceutical therapies; and technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs.

United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) seeks to travel down the corridors of indifference to develop treatments for rare, deadly diseases. We were founded in 1996 by a family seeking a cure for their daughter’s pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Today, we have six FDA-approved therapies that treat PAH, pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and neuroblastoma, a rare pediatric cancer. Our near-term pipeline seeks to develop additional therapies for PAH and pulmonary fibrosis (PF).

The cure for end-stage life-threatening diseases like PAH, PH-ILD, PF, and many others is an organ transplant, but only a small percentage of donated organs are available to address the vast need. For this reason, we are working to create manufactured organs to address the shortage of kidneys, hearts, lungs, and livers available for transplant. We believe an unlimited supply of tolerable, transplantable organs will eliminate the transplant waiting list and cure end-stage organ diseases for which transplant is not currently an option.

Who You Are

You are a strategic healthcare policy and reimbursement leader with deep expertise navigating the evolving U.S. healthcare landscape and translating complex policy developments into actionable business strategies. You bring extensive experience analyzing federal and state healthcare policies, CMS programs, legislative and regulatory changes, and payer dynamics to drive patient access, reimbursement success, and commercial performance. Known for your ability to anticipate emerging risks and opportunities, you partner cross-functionally with Market Access, HEOR, Government Pricing, Commercial, Legal, and Compliance teams to shape evidence generation, reimbursement readiness, and lifecycle planning strategies. A collaborative and forward-thinking leader, you combine sharp analytical skills, business acumen, and deep reimbursement expertise to ensure policy insights translate into meaningful outcomes for patients and the business.

title: eCommerce Manager
description:
At Local Crafts, we're the creative force behind some of the most beloved names in crafting—Connecting Threads, Superior Threads, Knit Picks, Crochet.com, and Berroco. From our own workshops to trusted partners around the globe, we design and curate products makers reach for every day: the fabrics, threads, yarns, and tools that turn ideas into finished pieces.

This is a new role, and a chance to shape how we experiment across our entire portfolio. As our E-Commerce Manager, you'll own testing across our brand websites—setting the roadmap, building and launching tests, and turning what you learn about our makers into lasting gains in conversion and revenue. It's a role for one curious, high-agency person who wants to see their work show up directly in how our customers shop and how our brands grow.

What You'll Do

* Own the conversion rate optimization strategy and testing roadmap across our brand websites, prioritizing by revenue impact and grounding every idea in customer conversations and data
* Design A/B tests across the full shopping journey, from homepage and navigation to product pages, cart, and checkout
* Scale what works across the portfolio while adapting for each brand's customer—a quilter on Connecting Threads doesn't shop like a knitter on Knit Picks
* Own the path to production for winning experiences, making sure every test launches cleanly, is tracked accurately, and gets rolled out to the live site
* Roll up your sleeves to get ideas across the finish line, from mocking up designs in Figma to building test variants or landing pages yourself with tools like Claude Code (with Engineering support when you need it)
* Analyze results with rigor, explain them in plain language—what happened, why, and how big the impact was—and build a shared learning library so every experiment adds to what we know about our makers
* Report on sessions, conversion rate, AOV, and funnel health, turn the data into clear, sized recommendations, and partner with the team on site merchandising and the overall site experience

What You'll Bring:

* 3–4 years in DTC e-commerce, including at least 2 years owning a testing program
* Hands-on experience with A/B testing tools, e-commerce platforms, and web analytics
* A revenue-driven approach rooted in the customer: you prioritize tests by business impact and you're confident analyzing results and explaining what they mean
* A builder's instinct—you'd rather build the thing than write the ticket
* Strong organization across multiple concurrent projects

You'll Thrive Here If:

* You're naturally curious about why a test wins, and you use that understanding to decide where to take it next
* You want your work to move the needle across a whole portfolio of brands, not just a single site
* You've managed CRO across several brands at once—or you're excited to learn how each customer base shops differently
* You're comfortable in front-end code like HTML, CSS, or JavaScript
* You knit, crochet, quilt, or have another connection to fiber crafts (not required, but you'll fit right in!)

Additional Information:

* This is a new, remote role open to candidates in the United States, reporting directly to the CRM & Lifecycle Director.
* Comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; paid time off; and parental leave.
* Employee discounts across all Local Crafts brands—Connecting Threads, Superior Threads, Knit Picks, Crochet.com, and Berroco.
* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States; Local Crafts is unable to sponsor employment visas for this position.

title: Marketing Coordinator
description:
The Marketing Coordinator is the day-to-day support engine for the DWC marketing department. This role keeps marketing running by managing social media posting, the swag closet, print production, event logistics, and the administrative needs of the team. The Coordinator produces content drafts with AI tools under the direction of the Director of Marketing and helps sales get the materials they need through the marketing ticketing system. The ideal candidate is organized, curious, eager to learn, and comfortable working across sales, operations, and outside vendors.

**Duties/Responsibilities**

* Schedule and publish posts across DWC social media channels; keep a consistent posting cadence and coordinate culture content from distribution center contributors (team highlights, cookouts, facility news).

* Support sales enablement review cycles: keep the review tracker current, send reviewers clear deadlines and reminders, and flag stalled items to the Director of Marketing.

* Provide logistics support for company and customer events, including the annual NASCAR hospitality event: hotel bookings, tickets, travel arrangements, and shipping of materials and swag.
* Supply Regional Sales Managers with swag, materials, and event kits for smaller, RSM-led customer events.
* Handle administrative needs of the marketing department, including vendor setup, purchase orders, invoice processing, expense tracking, meeting scheduling, and file organization.
* Support website and customer portal content updates as directed, including user testing and gathering feedback from internal reviewers.
* Maintain the brand asset library and confirm materials in circulation follow current brand standards.
* Track and report basic marketing metrics such as social engagement, ticket volume, and swag and print spend.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Required Skills/Abilities**

* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple requests and deadlines at once.
* Strong attention to detail and follow-through.
* Working knowledge of LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and social media scheduling tools.
* Comfortable using AI writing tools and willing to learn new technology quickly.
* Proficiency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office; experience with Canva or Adobe Creative Suite a plus.
* Ability to work professionally with sales, operations, leadership, and outside vendors.
* Curious, eager to learn, and takes initiative.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, or related field preferred.
* 0 to 2 years of experience in marketing, communications, or administrative support; internships count.
* Experience with HubSpot or other CRM and marketing automation platforms a plus.
* Experience in a B2B, manufacturing, or distribution environment a plus.

**Physical Requirements**

* Travel: Occasional travel for company and customer events, approximately 1 to 2 times per year.
* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to occasionally lift, push or pull 25 pounds (swag, print, and event materials), occasional bending and reaching.
* Must be able to pass a background check and drug screen.

**Pay Range:** $26/hour plus bonus potential

**Some reasons you want to work at DWC**

* Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance
* Company paid Life

* 401k
* Excellent time off options

* The work that you do matters

title: Director, Identity & Access Management
description:
Mylan Inc.

Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases.

We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making.

Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the role will make an impact:

The Director, Identity and Access Management (IAM) provides strategic leadership and enterprise oversight for the global IAM function and is a member of the Global Security leadership team, reporting to the Chief Security Officer. The Director establishes and leads the organization responsible for designing, building, operating, and continuously improving enterprise identity and access capabilities. The role directs identity governance, authentication, authorization, privileged access, identity lifecycle management, and secure integration of business applications and services. The Director partners with business and technology leaders to reduce identity-related risk, support regulatory obligations, improve user experience, and enable secure business operations.

Key responsibilities for this role include:

* Develop and execute the enterprise IAM strategy, operating model, roadmap, and standards aligned with business priorities and security objectives.
* Build, lead, and develop a global IAM organization accountable for architecture, engineering, delivery, operations, and service improvement.
* Direct enterprise identity lifecycle processes, including onboarding, changes, offboarding, provisioning, and deprovisioning across workforce and non-workforce identities.
* Oversee authentication, authorization, federation, single sign-on, and modern access controls to provide secure and usable access to enterprise resources.
* Lead privileged access management and identity governance capabilities, including entitlement management, access approvals, certifications, and segregation of duties.
* Ensure IAM architectures, technology selection, and integrations meet enterprise security requirements and support scalable, reliable service delivery.
* Establish IAM service performance, risk, and control measures; report progress, issues, and priorities to the Chief Security Officer and senior leadership.
* Direct IAM investment planning, budgets, resources, and delivery priorities while improving automation, operational efficiency, and service resilience.
* Partner with Human Resources, IT, application owners, and business leaders to integrate identity lifecycle and access decisions into business processes.
* Collaborate with security architecture, operations, privacy, compliance, and audit teams to embed IAM controls and address identity-related risks and findings.
* Support enterprise transformation, application onboarding, and organizational change by defining secure identity integration and access requirements.
* Promote adoption of IAM policies, secure authentication practices, and role-based training through stakeholder engagement and communications.
* Coordinate with technology and business continuity teams to maintain the availability and recovery readiness of critical identity services.

The minimum qualifications for this role are:

* Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree with a focus in MIS ,IT or Engineering or equivalent is required. Masters degree in MIS, IT, Engineering or related is preferred. Related experience and/or education may be considered.
* Minimum of ten years of IT or Cybersecurity experience is required. IAM – CISSP, CISM, CIAM, CIMP, or equivalent identity and access management certification preferred.
* Knowledge of enterprise IAM principles, identity lifecycle governance, access control models, and cybersecurity and privacy requirements.
* Knowledge of authentication and authorization methods, federation, single sign-on, and privileged access security concepts.
* Knowledge of security architecture, integration patterns, and evolving technologies supporting enterprise identity services.
* Knowledge of risk management, security controls, and governance requirements for access to sensitive business systems and information.
* Knowledge of IAM service delivery, operational resilience, and the business impacts of identity control failures.
* Knowledge of applicable cybersecurity, privacy, and regulatory obligations in a global, highly regulated enterprise.
* Ability to advise and influence senior company management on IAM strategy, identity-related risks, and investment priorities to support informed business decisions.
* Proven ability to partner with business management to deliver efficient, effective IAM solutions that meet operational needs and align with company objectives.
* Ability to lead global teams, manage organizational change, and establish accountability for service performance and continuous improvement.
* Skill in developing enterprise IAM strategies, roadmaps, and pragmatic solutions to complex access management challenges.
* Skill in evaluating identity-related risks, control effectiveness, and remediation priorities across enterprise systems.
* Skill in assessing IAM architectures, integrations, and technical control designs against business and security requirements.

Exact compensation may vary based on items such as skills, experience and location. The salary range for this position is: $112,000 - $236,000.

title: Senior Clinical Quality of Care RN - Arizona
description:
At UnitedHealthcare, we're simplifying the health care experience, creating healthier communities and removing barriers to quality care. The work you do here impacts the lives of millions of people for the better. Come build the health care system of tomorrow, making it more responsive, affordable and optimized. Ready to make a difference? Join us in making healthcare work better for everyone through people-led, responsible AI while **Caring. Connecting. Growing together.**

The Senior Clinical Quality of Care RN will be responsible for conducting quality of care (QOC) investigations, review and management of the regulatory Incident/Accident/Death (IAD) portal, documenting and communicating findings from these reviews utilizing state AHCCC and UHC technology platforms, and preparing reports or summaries for internal and external customers. This position collaborates with the Chief Medical Officer and other Medical Directors to review QOC and other investigations and ensures that QOC investigations comply with all applicable State, Federal, and regulatory requirements. Timely, professional and independent regulator correspondence is a core expectation. These activities are used to ensure care and services provided to our members are timely, adequate, and compliant with regulatory and professional standards and guidelines.

These QOC investigations are specific to Arizona Medicaid and Medicare members.

This position is an Arizona based remote position with the option of working 40% in-office. There is travel up to 25% of the time based on business needs and current regulatory case referrals. The office is located at 1 East Washington Street in Phoenix.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* Perform clinical documentation review of inpatient and outpatient care delivered to adults and children with Medicaid, Medicare health care benefits through Arizona United Health Care Community Plans for peer review and internal investigations of Quality of Care concerns
* Create professionally written case investigation summaries for Peer Review, present case summaries at the Provider Advisory Committee as applicable
* Review plans of correction from providers in response to a substantiated QOC occurrence
* Effectively interface with external customers, facilities and providers to resolve quality of care concerns, obtain medical records and other information
* Conduct delegated oversight reviews of contractors that perform work on behalf of UnitedHealthcare. This includes reviewing samples of contractor work against an audit tool or information found in medical charts
* Collaborate internally with Medical Directors and staff in other UHCCP departments
* Manage multiple tasks and projects and changing priorities; prioritize work products effectively
